task_name: the plan events vocabulary is `writing` and `ready` only

rubric.result: The objective promises that `reviewing` leaves the plan state on both sides of the wire so the stream can emit nothing but the two surviving frames. Taken apart and located: backend value object — `PlanStateValue` is `'writing' | 'ready'` and `PlanState` declares only `WRITING`/`READY` (plan-state.ts); application — `ReadPlanProgress` can no longer produce a third value, `#stateOf` is `this.planProgress.of({located, issue, repository})` and `#underReview`/`#momentOf` are gone; composition root — `CtApi.#readPlanProgress(git)` no longer builds or takes a review log. Wire — `PlanEvents.frameFor(state: PlanStateValue)` (plan-events-route.ts:146) is the stream's only writer of `state` and its parameter is now the two-member union, so a third frame is not constructible; `stream()` yields only `PlanEvents.frameFor(read.state)` where `read.state` is `PlanStateValue`. Frontend — `PlanEvents.types.ts` `PlanState` is the same two, `usePlanProgress` drops the `reviewing` phase, `PlanProgress.tsx` drops `onReviewing`, `REWORKING_MESSAGE`, the effect and the rendered line, `PlanEventsMother.reviewing` and `Home.planReviewing` with both `onReviewing=` props are gone. `grep -rl reviewing backend/src frontend/src` is empty in the worktree. On the slice's declared observability signal: no log line, metric or instrumentation was added anywhere in the diff — the only addition is one test; the signal rides the `state` field `frameFor` already emitted, which is what the desired end state prescribes ('no new log line is added'). Nothing the objective promises is missing.

The `**TDD:**` line names `it('the_state_of_a_plan_is_one_of_exactly_two_and_reviewing_is_not_one_of_them')` in `read-plan-progress.test.ts` and fixes the assertion as `Object.values(PlanState)` equals `['writing', 'ready']`. The diff adds exactly that test at read-plan-progress.test.ts:61-63 with body `expect(Object.values(PlanState)).toEqual(['writing', 'ready'])` — same assertion (`toEqual`, order included), same input (`Object.values(PlanState)` over the real imported value object, not a double), same expected value. It was red before this diff, where `PlanState` held three static members. No divergence.

Compared name by name. `Contract (read-plan-progress.ts)`: `readonly planProgress: PlanProgress` present; `constructor({ planProgress }: { planProgress: PlanProgress })` present verbatim; `execute(params: ReadPlanProgressParams)` still returns the declared result object carrying `readonly state: PlanStateValue`. The accompanying sentence — '`#underReview` and `#momentOf` go with the `reviewLog` collaborator and the `ReviewLog` import' — is honoured: all four are gone from the production module (the `ReviewLog` import that remains is in the test file, for the surviving port-default test, which is a different file). '`CtApi.#readPlanProgress` loses its `log` parameter' — signature is now `static #readPlanProgress(git: LaunchTool): ReadPlanProgress` and the call site is `CtApi.#readPlanProgress(git)`. '`PlanProgress.tsx` drops `onReviewing`, `REWORKING_MESSAGE`, the effect that calls it and the line that renders it' — all four removed. '`Home.tsx` drops `planReviewing` and both `onReviewing=` props' — done, both call sites. '`PlanEventsMother` drops `reviewing`' — the factory and the export entry both go. `Current state` blocks for plan-state.ts and usePlanProgress.ts matched the previous text and the diff removes exactly the third member from each. Constants: `PlanState.WRITING = 'writing'` and `READY = 'ready'` keep their literal values. The dropped `await` in `#stateOf` is what the closed-decision row spells literally ('`#stateOf` is `this.planProgress.of({ located, issue, repository })` and nothing else') and `execute` awaits the promise, so the returned value is unchanged.

Rows this diff bears on, each checked against the value stated. 'What `PlanState` becomes' — `export type PlanStateValue = 'writing' | 'ready'` and a class with exactly `WRITING` and `READY`; the frontend's `PlanState` becomes the same two: implemented as written. 'What `ReadPlanProgress` becomes' — `new ReadPlanProgress({ planProgress })`, no `reviewLog`, no `#underReview`, no `#momentOf`, `#stateOf` is the single port call: implemented as written. 'What the frontend loses' — this task's share (the `reviewing` phase of `usePlanProgress`, `PlanProgress`'s `onReviewing` prop and `REWORKING_MESSAGE`, `PlanEventsMother.reviewing`, `Home`'s `planReviewing`) all leave; the rest of that row belongs to other tasks and is left alone. 'Where the two halves of a contract move together' — `reviewing` leaves backend and frontend in this one task/commit, which is the value the row states. 'Which suite covers the surviving watch ... No task may modify it' — `pull-request-review-loop.test.ts` is not among the touched paths. 'The test commands' — the four commands are the ones the controls ran. No row is reopened or implemented with a different value.

Exemplars: `read-implementation-progress.ts` is named as 'an application query with a single port collaborator, which is what `ReadPlanProgress` becomes' — the diff leaves `ReadPlanProgress` with exactly one constructor-injected port, a declared params object and a declared result object, matching that idiom. `ImplementProgress.tsx` ('a component that renders a state vocabulary with no retired member') — `PlanProgress.tsx` now renders one line per surviving phase with no leftover branch and no catch-all. Rules opened and read from `plugin/conventions/`: defects.md, style.md, simplicity.md, decisions.md, domain.md, architecture.md, boundaries.md, testing.md; plus `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` (English on every surface bar frontend product copy — the only Spanish left in the diff's surroundings is rendered copy, and the removed `REWORKING_MESSAGE` was exactly that; the new test name is English) and `backend/conventions/this-repository.md` (TypeScript, layout unchanged).

`conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule, all four:
(1) Closed vocabulary — subject present, and the diff improves it. `PlanState`/`PlanStateValue` stays a closed vocabulary and loses a member; no string comparison by hand and no catch-all branch is introduced (`usePlanProgress` maps `state` straight to `phase`, `PlanProgress.tsx` has one guarded line per phase, no default). The diff also deletes `async #underReview(...): Promise<boolean>`, which was a boolean derived from the vocabulary to classify a state — the exact antipattern 'a boolean where the consumer needs to tell two states apart'. Conforme.
(2) Raw map as the return value of logic — `execute` still returns `ReadPlanProgressResult`, not a map; the only map is `JSON.stringify({ state })` inside `PlanEvents.frameFor`, the last step before the wire and untouched here. Conforme.
(3) Two fields that have to agree / sentinel — no subject introduced, and one is removed: `#underReview` derived the third state by agreeing `reviewLog.lastAskedAt` (a `string | null` date sentinel) with `planProgress.committedAt`, and after this diff the state comes from a single source. Conforme.
(4) An error named for where it happens — no error is added, renamed or reparented in this diff. No subject.

Two clashes declared here rather than reported as findings, because in each the plan's own text is what forbids the alternative and the implementer answers for neither:
(a) `conventions/testing.md` antipattern 'a test of the domain reachable from the application layer' — the new test asserts `Object.values(PlanState)` directly rather than through the use case. The `**TDD:**` line prescribes that exact assertion verbatim and rubric item 2 requires it, so no other diff was available.
(b) `conventions/simplicity.md` 'a public symbol, a parameter or a default with no caller' — with `#underReview` gone, `PlanProgress.committedAt` (domain port), `PlanContractProgress.committedAt` and `committedAtArgvFor` lose their last production reader; they keep only their adapter tests (`plan-contract-progress.test.ts:156-182`). Removing them would need `plan-progress.ts` and `plan-contract-progress.ts`, which are not in this task's `**Files:**`, and would contradict the closed row that fixes `#stateOf`. The plan declared the same consequence for `ReviewLog.lastAskedAt`/`MemoryReviewLog` in `### Out of scope` but did not declare this one — that is a gap in the plan, not in the diff. Worth a person's eye when the slice closes.

Delivery: the only rule of either yardstick that prescribes a shape of change here is `conventions/decisions.md` on the two halves of a contract that crosses a process boundary, and the plan closed it as 'in one commit'. The diff moves backend and frontend together, so the wire never carries half the vocabulary. Boundaries: no import direction changes (the application module now imports only domain types), no cast, no adapter policy, and the composition root stays the only place assembling the graph.

Three test files carry `-` lines, and every removed assertion, case or test traces to the task's own text.

`plan-events-route.test.ts`: one line, `expect(PlanEvents.frameFor(PlanState.REVIEWING)).toBe('data: {"state":"reviewing"}\n\n')`. The `**Tests:**` line names 'the `reviewing` frame case of `plan-events-route.test.ts`'. The surviving assertion still pins the literal SSE frame for `READY`, so the test can still fail for the reason its name gives.

`PlanProgress.test.tsx`: the three tests removed are named one by one in `**Tests:**`. `should not tell its parent a review started when the plan is merely ready` also carried `expect(onReady).toHaveBeenCalled()`, but that behaviour keeps its own test (`should call onReady once the plan reaches the ready state`), which survives untouched. The `renderProgress` helper losing `onReviewing` is forced by the `Contract` sentence '`PlanProgress.tsx` drops `onReviewing`'.

`read-plan-progress.test.ts`: this is the one that goes beyond `**Tests:**` — the whole `a plan being reworked is told apart from one waiting for a person` describe (8 tests) plus the `Flow`/`FlowReviewLog`/`FlowPlanProgress` helpers and their module constants, where the line names only the three `PlanState.REVIEWING` cases. I rule it forced, on two grounds that are in the task's own text. First, every one of the 8 runs through `Flow.run()`, whose body is `new ReadPlanProgress({ planProgress: this.planProgress, reviewLog: this.reviewLog })`; against the `Contract` block's `constructor({ planProgress }: { planProgress: PlanProgress })` that object literal is an excess property and does not compile, and `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` is one of the task's own verification commands. Second, the five beyond the three all assert the `#underReview`/`#momentOf` decision that the `Contract` block and the closed row 'What `ReadPlanProgress` becomes' delete outright — `a_plan_nobody_asked_changes_for...` asserts `reviewLog.askedFor`, `..._before_the_plan_was_recommitted...` and `..._in_the_very_second...` assert the date comparison, `a_date_that_cannot_be_read_as_a_moment...` and `a_commit_date_that_cannot_be_read...` assert `#momentOf`. A test of a mechanism the task removes has nothing left to pin. Nothing the repo still needs lost its only test: `PlanContractProgress.committedAt` keeps its four adapter cases at `plan-contract-progress.test.ts:156-182`; `ReviewLog`'s port defaults keep `a_port_that_nobody_implemented_says_so_instead_of_answering_undefined`, which the implementer deliberately left standing with both its `ReviewLog` assertions; `MemoryReviewLog` keeps all five of its own tests; the `PlanProgress` port default for `of` and `committedAt` is still asserted in the same surviving test. No assertion was quietly relaxed.

The promised behaviour is produced by production code, not by scaffolding. The two-member vocabulary lives in `backend/src/domain/value-objects/plan-state.ts`; the query that can no longer answer a third value lives in `backend/src/application/queries/read-plan-progress.ts`; the wiring that no longer carries a review log lives in `backend/src/infrastructure/ct-api.ts`; the frontend half lives in `PlanEvents.types.ts`, `usePlanProgress.ts`, `PlanProgress.tsx` and `Home.tsx`. The one new test asserts against the real imported `PlanState` — revert `plan-state.ts` alone and `Object.values(PlanState)` becomes `['writing','ready','reviewing']` and the test fails. The only scaffolding touched is `PlanEventsMother` (a `__scenarios__` mother) and the `renderProgress` helper, and both only lose what the production change removed. No mock, stub or hard-coded expected value stands in for a production line.

Every line written inside the declared files serves a sentence of the task: the vocabulary narrowing, the constructor and wiring it forces, the frontend half named in the `Contract` paragraph, and the one test the `**TDD:**` line prescribes. No refactor, rename, extra helper or adjacent fix rides along — the `+` lines are eleven, and each is either a signature the contract states or the prescribed test. `### Out of scope` checked by name: `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews` is byte for byte as it was, `log: new MemoryReviewLog()` included (ct-api.ts:320, outside every hunk of the diff); `RequestFixes`/`ReadFixesAsked` untouched; `ReviewWatch`, the `ReviewLog` port and `memory-review-log.ts` are not among the touched paths and both keep their files and their tests — the diff did not quietly take them with it, which is what the out-of-scope row declares. The `MemoryReviewLog` import in `ct-api.ts` is correctly kept, since the surviving wiring still needs it. `backend/API.md` still documents the `reviewing` frame and was correctly left alone: that is Task 8's `**Files:**`, and the desired end state is context, not a licence. No plan file appears in the diff, so there is no amendment to rule on.

One new test in the diff: `the_state_of_a_plan_is_one_of_exactly_two_and_reviewing_is_not_one_of_them` (read-plan-progress.test.ts:61). Deterministic — no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem, no randomness, no sleep; it reads a frozen set of static members. Isolated — it mutates nothing, shares no state, needs no order and builds everything it touches from the import. Verifies real behaviour — the assertion is on the production value object itself, not on a double or a constant the test defined; revert `plan-state.ts` and it fails. All three hold. Loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` to measure the finer half against the text the implementer was given: the test is one behaviour, its name is a sentence about what is guaranteed rather than a method name, and it uses real code with no mock, so nothing in that skill or in the `testing-anti-patterns.md` it names is contradicted. The one thing I could pin — `conventions/testing.md`'s 'a test of the domain reachable from the application layer' — is prescribed verbatim by the `**TDD:**` line, so it is declared under `patrones` and not reported here.
